notes: First backfill batch: July 2026, reached by search rather than by the feed, which only spans five days. The candidate stories were surfaced by an assisting model with web access; every URL, headline, publication date and quoted span below was re-fetched and checked against the live article before it was written here, and four findings the assisting pass missed inside an article it had already opened were added by that check.

coverage.note: Fourteen Mission Local articles published between 1 and 31 July 2026 were opened and read in full, across two assisted passes whose output was verified article by article. Thirteen distinct numbered San Francisco addresses appear across them; eleven carry a fact about the building. One article — the 10 July 'Mission Buzz' column — accounts for seven of the eleven. Counts record articles that can be audited, not the totals the passes claimed (18 and 15).
coverage.remaining: July is not exhausted. Two passes reached the address-shaped stories that searches surfaced, not the roughly 180 stories Mission Local published in the month; 25–31 July is still thin, and the second pass overlapped the first on one article rather than extending the window. The remaining Buzz columns are the densest thing left unread.

publish.note: The headline names the building's longtime owner, and the module's rule is categorical: a headline naming someone who is not an architect, builder, developer or firm cannot go on a page, and a headline may never be edited. The article describes him as the owner and a former permit expediter, which is not one of the permitted roles, and the buyer is described only by trade. So the entry cannot be written and no page is seeded. This one is worth a human's second look: he is a public figure in the city's permitting history rather than a private resident, and if that reading wins, the story is publishable as it stands and the parcel is 3531028.

findings.description: A Bayview public-housing complex is reported in decay. Recorded as rejected: the story gives no street address for the building, and it is about the people living in it.

citation.label: Mission Local, “While S.F. officials watched, a public-housing complex once considered a model spiraled out of control,” 23 July 2026

raw.text: At the 2700 building, [a resident] was left dead in his apartment for over a week, according to residents.

resolution.note: No usable address. The assisted pass reported “2700 Arelious Walker Drive”; the article names “the 2700 building” in one place and “Arelious Walker Drive” in another, several paragraphs apart, and never joins them. The quoted span it supplied for that address does not appear in the article at all — it reads as a description of a photograph. Nothing here resolves.

publish.note: Rejected on privacy before the address question is even reached. The story is about residents' living conditions and includes a death in an apartment, named. The root AGENTS.md forbids naming or describing residents, and news/AGENTS.md says a building's page is not a crime blotter. The raw span is redacted here for the same reason. The first assisted pass declined this same article correctly; the second promoted it to a finding.

extra.headline: While S.F. officials watched, a public-housing complex once considered a model spiraled out of control

findings.description: Demolition began at the WWII-era Potrero Hill Terrace and Annex public-housing site, to run at least nine months. Recorded as rejected: a real building story that names no street address.

citation.label: Mission Local, “Photos: Potrero Hill Terrace and Annex demolished after years-long wait,” 14 July 2026

raw.text: The World War II-era complex, formerly run by the San Francisco Housing Authority, will be torn down over the course of at least nine months, according to the Mayor’s Office of Housing and Community Development.

resolution.note: No usable address. The assisted pass reported “1000 Potrero Avenue”; the article contains no street number anywhere — it is a photo essay naming the complex, not an address. A site that large is many parcels in any case, so there is no single page this belongs on. Its quoted span is verbatim and the story is genuine; only the address was invented.

publish.note: Nothing to publish without an address. Kept as the record that the story was read and considered — and as a live candidate: if a later story names a street number at the site, this is the fact waiting for it.

extra.headline: Photos: Potrero Hill Terrace and Annex demolished after years-long wait
extra.headline_note: The assisted pass reported this headline without its “Photos:” prefix. A headline is quoted verbatim or not at all, so the correction matters even where nothing is published.
